common_name: Black Beauty Plum (Dark-Skinned Amber-Fleshed Japanese Plum)

planting.note: Plant bare-root while dormant in early spring or in fall in mild climates in well-drained soil in full sun; provide a compatible Japanese plum pollinizer such as Santa Rosa nearby.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a compatible Japanese plum pollinizer nearby. Black Beauty is a Japanese-type plum grown for its striking dark purple-black skin, which encloses firm, amber-yellow flesh with a sweet, well-balanced flavor and good, meaty texture that holds up well to handling and eating fresh out of hand. The vigorous tree is a reliable commercial and home-orchard producer in California-style plum growing regions, valued for combining attractive dark color with genuinely good flavor rather than color alone. Thin fruit if the tree sets a heavy crop, and harvest once fruit yields slightly to gentle pressure and has developed full dark color, since plums ripen further off the tree but develop the best flavor with some vine-ripening first.

common_name: Catalina Plum (Dark Red-Purple California Japanese Plum)

planting.note: Plant bare-root while dormant in early spring or in fall in mild climates in well-drained soil in full sun; provide a compatible Japanese plum pollinizer such as Santa Rosa nearby.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a compatible Japanese plum pollinizer nearby. Catalina is a California Japanese plum producing dark red to purple-skinned fruit with sweet, juicy, amber flesh, ripening in mid-season and valued for reliable, heavy production alongside good eating quality. The vigorous tree performs well under standard commercial plum-growing conditions and has remained a solid choice for home orchardists wanting a dependable, attractive dark plum without the more particular care some specialty varieties demand. Thin fruit if a heavy crop sets, and harvest once fruit yields slightly to gentle pressure and reaches full color for the sweetest flavor.

common_name: Duarte Plum (Historic California Red-Fleshed Japanese Plum)

planting.note: Plant bare-root while dormant in early spring or in fall in mild climates in well-drained soil in full sun; provide a compatible Japanese plum pollinizer such as Santa Rosa nearby.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a compatible Japanese plum pollinizer nearby. Duarte is an early 20th-century California heirloom Japanese plum notable for red flesh streaked through the fruit's interior rather than the more common amber or yellow flesh of most Japanese plums, a striking trait when the fruit is cut open, paired with dark red skin and a rich, tangy-sweet flavor. Historically significant in early California plum breeding, it remains grown today by heirloom fruit enthusiasts and specialty orchards valuing its distinctive red-fleshed character and genuine history. Thin fruit if the tree sets heavily, and harvest once fruit yields slightly to gentle pressure and develops full color for the best flavor.

common_name: Queen Ann Plum (Large Sweet Dark Purple California Plum)

planting.note: Plant bare-root while dormant in early spring or in fall in mild climates in well-drained soil in full sun; provide a compatible Japanese plum pollinizer such as Santa Rosa nearby.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a compatible Japanese plum pollinizer nearby. Queen Ann is a California Japanese plum producing large, dark purple-black fruit with sweet, juicy, amber flesh, prized for its substantial size and dependable, heavy production in commercial and home orchard settings. The tree is vigorous and well suited to standard Japanese plum growing conditions, delivering fruit with good flavor balance and firm enough texture to handle well from harvest to table. Thin fruit if the tree sets a heavy crop to maintain good size, and harvest once fruit yields slightly to gentle pressure and reaches full dark color for the sweetest, best-developed flavor.

common_name: Wickson Plum (Luther Burbank's Sweet Crisp Yellow Plum)

planting.note: Plant bare-root while dormant in early spring or in fall in mild climates in well-drained soil in full sun; provide a compatible Japanese plum pollinizer such as Santa Rosa nearby.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a compatible Japanese plum pollinizer nearby. Wickson was bred by legendary plant breeder Luther Burbank in the early 1900s and named for a friend, producing translucent yellow-skinned fruit with an exceptionally high sugar content and crisp, dense flesh that has made it a favorite among chefs and farmers-market growers seeking intensely sweet, distinctive stone fruit. The plum's crisp texture, closer to an apple's crunch than the soft, juicy give of most plums, sets it apart texturally as well as in flavor, and it has enjoyed a revival of interest among specialty growers rediscovering Burbank's historic introductions. Thin fruit if the tree sets heavily, and harvest once fruit turns translucent gold and yields slightly to pressure for the sweetest flavor.
